methodological_rigor.justification: Post hoc pooled safety analysis with EAIR methodology, proper grading using NCI-CTCAE v4.03, and comparative analysis against ibrutinib from ALPINE trial. Authors acknowledge key limitations including retrospective nature and heterogeneous disease population. Exposure-adjusted incidence rates appropriately control for varying treatment durations. However, prespecified analyses would strengthen conclusions and power calculations are absent.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Zanubrutinib is FDA-approved and clinically used; safety profile directly informs treatment selection for Asian patients with B-cell malignancies. Comparative safety data versus ibrutinib has clear practice implications. Analysis of 406 Asian patients with extended follow-up (median 25 months, 38.7% with ≥36 months) provides real-world evidence for long-term management decisions.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods clearly describe patient selection, safety assessment definitions, EAIR calculation methodology, and baseline characteristics are well-reported in Table 1. Missing elements: explicit data cut-off rationale, formal handling of missing data statement, sensitivity analyses despite acknowledged heterogeneous population. Data availability noted as limited (supplementary tables referenced but content redacted in normalized version).

novelty_literature.justification: Analysis replicates findings from previous pooled safety analysis (ref 19) restricted to Asian subgroup without new mechanistic insights. Lower atrial fibrillation rates with zanubrutinib versus ibrutinib were previously demonstrated in ASPEN and ALPINE pivotal trials. This work adds geographic/demographic confirmation but lacks methodological or substantive innovation.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear results presentation. Informative tables (demographics, safety data) and figures (TEAE frequencies, EAIR comparisons over time) effectively communicate findings. EAIR visualization is clear. Some sections contain redundancy between abstract bullet points and introduction; supplementary table references are incomplete with [REDACTED] placeholders.

key_strengths: Clear head-to-head comparative analysis with ibrutinib from ALPINE trial
Exposure-adjusted incidence rates appropriately control for varying treatment durations across pooled trials
Diverse disease representation including CLL, MCL, WM, FL, DLBCL, and MZL
Extended follow-up with 38.7% of patients treated ≥36 months providing long-term safety data
Consistent safety profile findings with prior global population analysis suggests robust result
key_concerns: Limited novelty: largely replicates prior pooled analysis (Brown et al 2024, ref 19) in Asian subgroup without additional mechanistic understanding
No multiple comparison adjustment despite testing numerous adverse event endpoints
Confidence intervals not consistently reported for EAIR comparisons between groups
Small comparative cohort (45 zanubrutinib versus 43 ibrutinib) limits power for ALPINE subset analysis
Post hoc nature with heterogeneous disease populations; no prespecified sensitivity analyses
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent safety analysis with solid methodology and clear clinical relevance, but incremental novelty and retrospective design limit tier placement. Suitable for specialized tier 3 oncology journals that publish pharmacovigilance studies extending prior trials to specific populations.
